question: A 35-year-old man has a fistula-in-ano with the external opening in the right posterior quadrant of the perianal skin, at the 7 o'clock position. According to Goodsall's rule, the internal opening is most likely to be:

answers.text: Directly radially opposite at the 7 o'clock position in the anal canal — posterior openings follow a straight radial course

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Straight radial tracks are the rule for ANTERIOR external openings (below the 3–9 o'clock transverse line). Posterior external openings follow a curved course to a single internal opening at the posterior midline.

answers.text: At the 6 o'clock posterior midline of the anal canal — posterior external openings curve to the posterior midline internal opening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Goodsall's rule: external openings POSTERIOR to the transverse (3–9 o'clock) line → curved track → single internal opening at the posterior midline (6 o'clock). External openings ANTERIOR to the line → straight radial track → internal opening at corresponding position.

answers.text: At the 12 o'clock anterior midline — all posterior fistulae have an anterior internal opening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Posterior external openings point to the POSTERIOR midline (6 o'clock), not the anterior midline. Goodsall's rule specifies posterior external = posterior midline internal; anterior external = radial track to corresponding anterior position.

overallFeedback.feedback: Goodsall's rule: draw the 3–9 o'clock transverse line. External opening POSTERIOR to line → curved track to posterior midline (6 o'clock). External opening ANTERIOR to line → straight radial track. This guides surgery to find the internal opening.
Correct. Goodsall's rule: posterior external opening → curved track → 6 o'clock posterior midline internal opening. Anterior external opening → straight radial track.
